title: Server-side JSX with jsx-async-runtime
description: Everything jsx-async-runtime renders on the server: promises, iterables and other values as children, render props, request context via 'this', overriding how JSX turns into HTML, Declarative Shadow DOM and unit tests for components.

title: Streaming with jsx-async-runtime
description: Async components don't block the page: jsx-async-runtime streams HTML as soon as it is ready, in order, in parallel or out of order, from async iterables or a ReadableStream.

title: Isomorphic apps with jsx-async-runtime
description: The server renders the first page, then the browser re-renders the same JSX components after every click, without React, a virtual DOM or hydration. Without JavaScript, every app keeps working with plain HTML forms.

title: Client-side apps and games with jsx-async-runtime
description: Render JSX right in the browser with jsx-async-runtime: async components which fetch their own data, live feeds, streamed async trees, and games which render every frame.

title: Server-rendered websites and apps
description: Render pages on the server with content from a remote API, JSON data or Markdown with MDX, and build multi-step forms with plain HTML. No client-side JavaScript needed: view transitions make page changes feel smooth.

title: Beyond HTML: images, PDFs, emails and live streams
description: Routes aren't limited to HTML: they can return images, SVG, JSON, XML, PDF, a live stream of Server-Sent Events, a WebSocket or any other content type.

title: Security, errors and post-processing
description: Protect routes with basic auth or sessions, sign cookies, block injected scripts stop bots with a proof-of-work captcha and rate-limit APIs. Catch errors, manage the head and transform the final HTML before it is sent to the browser.

title: Hypermedia with HTMX
description: Every Jeasx route can return an HTML fragment, so hypermedia libraries like HTMX can update parts of a page with markup rendered on the server.

title: JavaScript libraries and frameworks
description: Add islands of interactivity to server-rendered pages with the JavaScript library or framework you already know.
